question: Who became the first woman to command the Armed Forces Transfusion Centre, Delhi Cantt, which is the largest blood transfusion centre of the Armed Forces in Nov 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Col Sunita BS.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In November 2023, Colonel Sunita BS became the first woman to command the Armed Forces Transfusion Centre (AFTC) at Delhi Cantt, the largest blood transfusion centre of the Armed Forces. (कर्नल सुनीता बी.एस.)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The AFTC collects, processes and supplies blood and blood products to armed forces hospitals across India.

• Her appointment marked a milestone for women in leadership roles in the Indian Army Medical Corps.

NOTE

• Women officers have been reaching many "firsts" in the armed forces recently, including command roles, fighter-pilot duties and permanent commission (following the 2020 Supreme Court verdict).

question: In which of the following classical dance forms are the actors' faces painted to symbolise the type of character they are playing?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kathakali.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In "Kathakali", the classical dance-drama of Kerala, the actors' faces are elaborately painted (make-up) to symbolise the type of character they play (e.g., Pacha/green for noble heroes, Kathi for villains). (कथकली — चेहरे की रंगाई)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Kathakali is known for its huge, colourful costumes, headgear and detailed facial make-up; it is largely performed by men and enacts stories from the Ramayana and Mahabharata.

• The make-up colours: Pacha (green) = virtuous, Kathi = villainous, Thadi = bearded types, Kari (black) = demonesses.

NOTE

• The eight classical dances: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (North India), Kathakali & Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur), Sattriya (Assam).

question: In 1992, which organisation launched Self Help Group – Bank Linkage Programme?
solution_text:
The correct answer is NABARD.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In 1992, "NABARD (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development)" launched the Self Help Group – Bank Linkage Programme (SHG-BLP) to connect informal Self Help Groups with the formal banking system for credit. (नाबार्ड — स्वयं सहायता समूह-बैंक लिंकेज कार्यक्रम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The SHG-Bank Linkage Programme is the largest microfinance programme in the world, promoting financial inclusion, especially among rural women.

• NABARD was established in 1982 as the apex bank for rural and agricultural credit.

NOTE

• Regulators/apex bodies: SEBI (securities market), RBI (central bank & monetary policy), NABARD (rural/agriculture refinance), SIDBI (small industries).

question: In which of the following states is the Bhadaravi Poonam Mela organised every year in the Nilkanth Mahadev temple premises in Babra?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gujarat.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Bhadaravi Poonam Mela" (also linked with the Ambaji fair) is organised every year in Gujarat. The question notes its association with the Nilkanth Mahadev temple premises in Babra. (गुजरात — भादरवी पूनम मेला)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The famous Bhadarvi Poonam Mela at Ambaji (Banaskantha, Gujarat) is one of the largest religious fairs in India, held on the full moon of the Bhadrapada month.

• Ambaji is one of the 51 Shakti Peethas, dedicated to Goddess Amba/Shakti.

NOTE

• Major fairs of India: Kumbh Mela (UP/Uttarakhand/MP), Pushkar Fair (Rajasthan), Sonepur Mela (Bihar), Ambaji/Bhadarvi Poonam Mela (Gujarat).

question: As per the Constitution (Ninety-First Amendment) Act, 2003, the total number of ministers, including the Prime Minister, shall NOT exceed:
option_1: 20% of the total number of members of the Lok Sabha
option_2: 15% of the total number of members of the Lok Sabha
option_3: 10% of the total number of members of the Lok Sabha
option_4: 25% of the total number of members of the Lok Sabha
solution_text:
The correct answer is 15% of the total number of members of the Lok Sabha.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Constitution (Ninety-First Amendment) Act, 2003, the total number of Ministers, including the Prime Minister, in the Council of Ministers shall NOT exceed 15% of the total number of members of the Lok Sabha. (91वां संविधान संशोधन — 15%)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The same 15% ceiling applies to the states (Article 164(1A)), but a state's Council of Ministers must have a minimum of 12 ministers.

• The 91st Amendment (2003) also strengthened the Anti-Defection Law (Tenth Schedule) by barring defectors from holding ministerial office.

NOTE

• Relevant Articles: Article 75(1A) (size of Union Council of Ministers) and Article 164(1A) (size in states).

question: Which of the following cities is known as the Steel City in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jamshedpur.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Jamshedpur" (in Jharkhand) is known as the "Steel City" of India. It grew around the Tata Iron and Steel Company (TISCO/Tata Steel), established in 1907 by Jamsetji Nusserwanji Tata. (जमशेदपुर — स्टील सिटी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Jamshedpur is also called "Tatanagar" and is regarded as the first planned industrial city of India.

• Other steel cities: Bhilai (Chhattisgarh), Bokaro (Jharkhand), Rourkela (Odisha), Durgapur (West Bengal).

NOTE

• City nicknames: Bengaluru – Silicon Valley of India; Detroit of India – Chennai; Manchester of India – Ahmedabad; Steel City – Jamshedpur.

question: Indian classical musician, Ustad Rashid Khan was awarded the Padma Bhushan in 2022 for his contribution to which of the following music categories?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hindustani classical music.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ustad Rashid Khan was awarded the Padma Bhushan in 2022 for his contribution to Hindustani classical music. He belonged to the Rampur–Sahaswan gharana. (हिंदुस्तानी शास्त्रीय संगीत)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Ustad Rashid Khan was famous for his khayal and thumri renditions; he passed away in January 2024.

• He was earlier honoured with the Padma Shri (2006) and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award.

NOTE

• Indian classical music has two main streams: Hindustani (North India) and Carnatic (South India). Padma awards: Padma Vibhushan > Padma Bhushan > Padma Shri.

question: In a metro station, it was observed that on an average 20 people per minute were using the escalator to reach at a height of 15 metres. Calculate the power of the escalator assuming the average mass of people to be 50 kg and acceleration due to gravity to be 10 m/s2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2.5 kW.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Power = Work done / time. Work done in lifting people = mgh (gain in potential energy).

◦ In 1 minute (60 s), 20 people are lifted, total mass = 20 × 50 = 1000 kg.

◦ Work = m g h = 1000 × 10 × 15 = 1,50,000 J.

◦ Power = Work / time = 1,50,000 ÷ 60 = 2500 W = 2.5 kW.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Power is the rate of doing work; SI unit is the watt (W); 1 kW = 1000 W.

• Potential energy = mgh, where m = mass, g = 10 m/s², h = height.

NOTE

• Useful relations: 1 horsepower (hp) ≈ 746 W; 1 kWh = 3.6 × 10⁶ J (the "unit" of electricity).

question: When was the Ustad Bismillah Khan Yuva Puraskar, an award given by the Sangeet Natak Akademi to outstanding artists under 40 who have demonstrated talent in the fields of music, dance and theatre, started?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2006.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Ustad Bismillah Khan Yuva Puraskar" was started in 2006 by the Sangeet Natak Akademi. It is given to outstanding young artists (under 40 years) in the fields of music, dance and theatre. (उस्ताद बिस्मिल्लाह खान युवा पुरस्कार — 2006)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• It is named after the legendary shehnai maestro Ustad Bismillah Khan, who was awarded the Bharat Ratna (2001).

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi (established 1952) is India's national academy for music, dance and drama.

NOTE

• Highest honour of the Akademi is the Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship (Ratna Sadasya); the Akademi Award is given for lifetime achievement.

question: Who among the following was the pioneer of 'Bhoodan Movement'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Acharya Vinoba Bhave.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Bhoodan Movement" (Land Gift Movement) was pioneered by Acharya Vinoba Bhave in 1951, starting from Pochampally village (Telangana). It appealed to landowners to voluntarily donate land to the landless. (आचार्य विनोबा भावे — भूदान आंदोलन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Vinoba Bhave was a follower of Mahatma Gandhi and was chosen by him as the first individual Satyagrahi (1940).

• The movement later expanded into the "Gramdan" (village-gift) movement.

NOTE

• Vinoba Bhave was the first recipient of the Ramon Magsaysay Award (1958) and was posthumously awarded the Bharat Ratna (1983).

question: In Dholavira, which of the following materials is extensively used as a building material?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Stone.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• At "Dholavira" (a Harappan site in Gujarat, in the Rann of Kutch), stone was extensively used as a building material, unlike most other Harappan sites that mainly used baked/mud bricks. (धौलावीरा — पत्थर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Dholavira is famous for its excellent water management system (reservoirs, dams), a unique three-part city plan (citadel, middle town, lower town) and a large signboard with Indus script.

• It was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2021.

NOTE

• Major Harappan sites: Harappa & Mohenjo-daro (Pakistan), Lothal, Dholavira, Rakhigarhi, Kalibangan, Ropar (India). Rakhigarhi (Haryana) is the largest Harappan site in India.

question: The concept of Concurrent List in the Indian Constitution is borrowed from the Constitution of _____________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Australia.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The concept of the "Concurrent List" in the Indian Constitution is borrowed from the Constitution of Australia. Both the Centre and the States can legislate on the subjects in this list. (समवर्ती सूची — ऑस्ट्रेलिया से)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Seventh Schedule of the Constitution has three lists: Union List, State List and Concurrent List.

• In case of a conflict on a Concurrent List subject, the Union law prevails (Article 254).

NOTE

• Borrowed features: Fundamental Rights, Judicial Review (USA); Parliamentary system, Rule of Law (Britain); Concurrent List, Freedom of Trade (Australia); Directive Principles (Ireland); Fundamental Duties, Planning (USSR).

question: What is the rank of Sri Lanka in the Global Hunger Index (GHI) 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 60.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the Global Hunger Index (GHI) 2023, Sri Lanka was ranked 60th among the countries assessed. (वैश्विक भूख सूचकांक 2023 — श्रीलंका 60वें स्थान पर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• India was ranked 111 out of 125 countries in the GHI 2023, placing it in the "serious" category.

• The GHI is jointly published by Concern Worldwide (Ireland) and Welthungerhilfe (Germany).

NOTE

• The GHI is measured on four indicators: undernourishment, child stunting, child wasting and child mortality. Lower score/rank = less hunger.

question: What is the primary acid found in citrus fruits like oranges and lemons?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Citric acid.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The primary acid found in citrus fruits like oranges and lemons is "citric acid", which gives them their sour/tangy taste. (साइट्रिक अम्ल — नींबू, संतरा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Lactic acid – found in curd/milk (sour milk) and muscles.

• Tartaric acid – found in tamarind and grapes.

• Acetic acid – found in vinegar.

NOTE

• Other natural acids: Malic acid (apple), Oxalic acid (tomato/spinach), Formic acid (ant sting/bee), Citric acid (citrus fruits).

question: In which state are the Gua and Noamundi iron ore mines located?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jharkhand.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Gua" and "Noamundi" iron ore mines are located in the West Singhbhum district of Jharkhand. Noamundi is one of the oldest mechanised iron ore mines in India, operated by Tata Steel. (झारखंड — गुआ और नोआमुंडी लौह अयस्क खदानें)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Jharkhand is very rich in minerals — iron ore, coal, mica, copper and uranium.

• India's major iron ore belts also lie in Odisha, Chhattisgarh and Karnataka (Bellary–Hospet).

NOTE

• Types of iron ore: Magnetite (best quality, ~72% iron), Hematite (most used commercially), Limonite and Siderite.

question: The climatic diversity of India is characterised by its distinctiveness, and one of the following factors does NOT contribute to it is ______________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is longitudinal extent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Among the given options, "longitudinal extent" does NOT significantly contribute to India's climatic diversity. Longitude mainly affects time (local time differences), not climate. Climate is more influenced by latitude, topography (relief) and vegetation. (देशांतरीय विस्तार — जलवायु को प्रभावित नहीं करता)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Latitudinal extent affects temperature (the Tropic of Cancer passes through the middle of India).

• Topography (Himalayas, Western Ghats) blocks/directs winds and rainfall; vegetation affects local humidity and temperature.

NOTE

• Key controls of Indian climate: latitude, altitude, pressure & winds (monsoons), distance from the sea, ocean currents and relief (topography).

question: The rock-cut temple of Shiva built by Krishna I is found at which of the following places?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ellora.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The famous rock-cut Kailasa Temple of Shiva, built by the Rashtrakuta king Krishna I, is found at "Ellora" (in Maharashtra). It is carved out of a single rock. (एलोरा — कैलाश मंदिर, कृष्ण प्रथम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Kailasa Temple (Cave 16) at Ellora is the world's largest monolithic rock-cut structure.

• The Ellora Caves (Buddhist, Hindu and Jain) are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

NOTE

• The Rashtrakutas (8th–10th century CE) had their capital at Manyakheta; Ellora and the Elephanta Caves are among their greatest architectural legacies.

question: Consider the following statements in the context of the Vedas. 1.The Vedas are called Shruti. 2.The Rigveda consists of ten Mandalas. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both 1 and 2.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Statement 1 is correct: The Vedas are called "Shruti" ("that which is heard"), as they were traditionally transmitted orally.

• Statement 2 is correct: The Rigveda consists of ten Mandalas (books). Hence both statements are correct. (दोनों कथन सही — वेद 'श्रुति', ऋग्वेद में 10 मंडल)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The four Vedas: Rigveda (hymns), Samaveda (melodies/chants), Yajurveda (sacrificial formulae), Atharvaveda (spells and charms).

• The Rigveda is the oldest Veda; its 3rd Mandala contains the Gayatri Mantra.

NOTE

• Vedic literature is classified as Shruti (Vedas, Brahmanas, Aranyakas, Upanishads) and Smriti (Puranas, epics, Dharmashastras).

question: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides provision for appointment of the same person as the Governor for two or more states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 153.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Article 153" of the Constitution provides that there shall be a Governor for each State; a proviso added by the 7th Amendment (1956) allows the same person to be appointed as the Governor for two or more states. (अनुच्छेद 153)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Article 155 – Governor is appointed by the President.

• Article 156 – tenure of the Governor (holds office during the pleasure of the President; normally 5 years).

• Article 157 – qualifications; Article 158 – conditions of the Governor's office.

NOTE

• The Governor is the constitutional head of a state (Articles 153–162). The office was borrowed from the Government of India Act, 1935 / Canadian model.

question: In which of the following year did India win the ICC T20 Men's Cricket World Cup?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2007.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India won the first-ever ICC T20 Men's Cricket World Cup in 2007, held in South Africa, defeating Pakistan in the final. The team was captained by Mahendra Singh Dhoni. (2007 — पहला टी20 विश्व कप, भारत विजेता)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• In the 2007 final, Joginder Sharma bowled the decisive last over; Yuvraj Singh famously hit six sixes in an over off Stuart Broad in that tournament.

• India won the T20 World Cup again in 2024 (in the West Indies & USA), captained by Rohit Sharma.

NOTE

• India's World Cup wins: 1983 & 2011 (ODI World Cup) and 2007 & 2024 (T20 World Cup); also the 2013 Champions Trophy.

question: Which of the following government initiatives focuses on skill development to reduce open unemployment among youth in India?
option_2: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY).

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY)" focuses on skill development to make the youth employable and reduce open unemployment. It was launched in 2015 under the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship. (प्रधानमंत्री कौशल विकास योजना)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• PM KUSUM – promotes solar energy for farmers.

• MGNREGA (2005) – guarantees 100 days of wage employment in rural areas.

• Swachh Bharat Abhiyan (2014) – cleanliness and sanitation mission.

NOTE

• PMKVY is implemented by the National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC); it offers Short-Term Training and Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL).

question: How many titles did West Bengal win in the Santosh Trophy events up to the 2022-23 season?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 32.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Up to the 2022–23 season, West Bengal had won the Santosh Trophy a record 32 times, making it the most successful team in the tournament. (संतोष ट्रॉफी — पश्चिम बंगाल, 32 खिताब)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Santosh Trophy is a national football championship contested by state associations and government institutions, started in 1941.

• It is named after Sir Manmatha Nath Roy Chowdhary of Santosh (now in Bangladesh).

NOTE

• Indian football bodies: AIFF (All India Football Federation) governs the game; the top club league is the Indian Super League (ISL).

question: Who among the following Governor-Generals declared 'Sati' practice as illegal?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lord William Bentinck.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Lord William Bentinck" declared the practice of "Sati" as illegal through the Bengal Sati Regulation Act of 1829. He was supported in this reform by Raja Ram Mohan Roy. (लॉर्ड विलियम बेंटिंक — सती प्रथा उन्मूलन, 1829)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Lord William Bentinck was the first Governor-General of India (1833–35) under the Charter Act of 1833.

• Other reforms in his time: suppression of Thuggee (with William Sleeman) and promotion of English education (Macaulay's Minute, 1835).

NOTE

• Lord Canning – last Governor-General & first Viceroy (Revolt of 1857); Lord Dalhousie – Doctrine of Lapse, railways; Lord Lytton – Vernacular Press Act, 1878.

question: Which of the following fictional towns is mentioned in the English novel 'In Custody' written by Anita Desai?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mirpore.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The fictional town "Mirpore" is mentioned in the novel "In Custody" written by Anita Desai (published 1984). The story follows a Hindi lecturer, Deven, and an Urdu poet, Nur. (मिरपोर — 'इन कस्टडी', अनीता देसाई)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• "In Custody" was shortlisted for the Booker Prize and later made into a film by Merchant–Ivory.

• Anita Desai is a noted Indian novelist; her works include Fire on the Mountain, Clear Light of Day and The Village by the Sea.

NOTE

• Famous fictional Indian towns: Malgudi (R. K. Narayan), Kanthapura (Raja Rao), Mirpore (Anita Desai), Lilliput (Jonathan Swift's Gulliver's Travels).

question: A particular cell present in the excretory system of flatworms, which helps them removing waste materials is the:
solution_text:
The correct answer is flame cell.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Flame cells" are the specialised excretory cells present in the excretory system of flatworms (Platyhelminthes) and some other invertebrates. They help remove waste materials and excess water (osmoregulation). (फ्लेम कोशिका — चपटे कृमि का उत्सर्जन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Flame cells are part of the protonephridia; the beating of their cilia (resembling a flickering flame) drives fluid through the system.

• In earthworms, the excretory organs are nephridia; in humans, the excretory unit is the nephron (in kidneys).

NOTE

• Cnidoblasts (nematocysts) are the stinging cells of Cnidaria (Hydra, jellyfish); passage cells occur in the endodermis of plant roots.
